title: SOC2 preflight dry-run: notes and action plan
content:
Context: quick scratchpad for the SOC2/ISO dry-run we plan to run with Maya and Omar before the customer audit. Intended audience: me (Jordan) and immediate collaborators. This is a working list - not final evidence set.

Goal for the session (45-60m):
- Walk through each high-risk control area to confirm evidence locations and owners
- Validate vendor attestation status for all critical subprocessors
- Run a quick tabletop for the incident response flow and confirm last tabletop date
- Identify urgent gaps that need remediation before the external auditor asks

High-level scope:
- Trust Services Criteria in-scope: Security (required), Availability (selected), Confidentiality (selected)
- ISO 27001 alignment: Annex A controls relevant to access control, cryptography, supplier relationships
- Vendors: cloud infra, key management, observability (SaaS), backup provider, code scanning vendor

Key control checkpoints (notes + evidence pointers):
1) Access management
- What to show: SSO + SCIM provisioning doc, list of active admins in Okta, MFA enforcement policy
- Evidence locations: Confluence (access-control-md), Okta export (okta-admins-2025-11-01.csv), IAM audit logs (s3 path above)
- Owner: Priya
- Questions: any stale service accounts? confirm last orphaned-account cleanup run (ticket JIRA-4678)

2) Secrets & encryption
- Show: KMS rotation policy, proof of CMK rotation date, encryption at rest config for DBs and object storage
- Evidence: KMS audit events (s3), DB config screens (screenshots in Confluence), PR that enabled server-side encryption (github link)
- Owner: Omar

3) Logging, monitoring, alerting
- Show: centralized logging retention policy, SIEM/alerting runbook, sample alert-to-ticket flow
- Evidence: alerting runbook doc, sample pagerduty incident (PD-8901), Grafana dashboard snapshots
- Owner: Maya

4) Change management / deploy controls
- Show: PR review policy, producer/consumer of release notes, rollback playbook
- Evidence: GitHub protected branch settings, release tags list, change ticket template (JIRA-3012)
- Owner: Eng leads (linked in Confluence)

5) Vendor risk / third-party assurance
- Focus first on: cloud infra provider, KMS provider, observability vendor, code scanning vendor
- Ask: do we have SOC2 Type II or ISO certificates from each? any open issues in vendor risk portal?
- Evidence: vendor attestation folder (confluence link), contracts redlines summary (legal), vendor risk tickets (JIRA-VEND-102)
- Action: confirm we have updated subprocessors list in privacy policy; if not, add as action

6) Incident response & tabletop
- Walkthrough: detection -> triage -> containment -> notification -> postmortem
- Evidence: last tabletop doc (date 2025-06-10), incident timeline template, public notification checklist
- Gap check: confirm communication chain to customers and sales for PII incidents

7) Data flows & classification
- Show: data flow diagrams for hosted API and Dedicated customers, classification matrix mapping fields to confidentiality
- Evidence: api-dataflow-v2 confluence page, data class examples, DB column classification csv
- Owner: Product eng

Open risks / expected auditor focus
- Vendor attestations: two vendors lack current Type II (observability vendor & backup provider)
- Secrets sprawl: a couple of legacy Jenkins jobs still storing tokens in plaintext (ticket JENK-92)
- Retention mismatch: logging retention shorter than stated in policy for one region
- Backup encryption: confirm backup provider uses customer-managed keys (requires contract clause)

Pre-meeting checklist (what I will bring to dry-run):
- One-page control matrix (quick view by owner + evidence path)
- Links to evidence buckets and Confluence pages (copied into the meeting chat)
- Short script for the tabletop (detection scenario + expected timers)
- List of 3 immediate actions I can take right after the meeting

Proposed meeting agenda (30-45m compact):
- 0-5m: quick goals and what we expect to show
- 5-25m: rapid walk through 4 highest risk control areas (access, secrets, vendor risk, incident response)
- 25-35m: tabletop run (15m) if time permits
- 35-45m: assign owners for gaps, set rough ETA, and confirm where evidence will be consolidated

Immediate follow-ups (assigned):
- Priya: export Okta admin list + run orphaned account cleanup job (ETA: 2025-11-15)
- Omar: pull KMS rotation logs and confirm backup key ownership with vendor (ETA: 2025-11-18)
- Maya: snapshot critical dashboards and attach to runbook; verify SIEM retention (ETA: 2025-11-14)
- Jordan (me): consolidate the evidence index page, ping legal for vendor attestation status, schedule vendor outreach (ETA: 2025-11-13)

Longer-term items (post dry-run):
- Formalize vendor attestation tracker and add to monthly compliance dashboard
- Schedule a full audit prep run 4 weeks before the auditor's start date
- Build a short 'evidence pack' template per control so we can hand over quickly

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc light; move finalized evidence list to Confluence under /SEC/soc2/evidence once validated
- Remember to tag tickets with 'soc2-blocker' so we can filter easily
- For tabletop, pick a realistic service outage scenario that exercises cross-team comms (eg: KV cache bug causing elevated error rates)

Links to pull into meeting chat:
- Confluence controls matrix: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/controls-matrix
- Evidence S3 path: s3://redwood-audit-bucket/soc2/evidence/
- Vendor attestations folder: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/Vendor+Attestations
- JIRA board: https://jira.redwood.com/secure/RapidBoard.jspa?rapidView=78

End of scratchpad: convert to a formal meeting note after the dry-run and move to shared_drives if we want to publicize across teams.
